items.title: refusals: one throw answers one declared sentence — an action that refuses a selection for several reasons at once cannot list them in the person's language (after #34273)
items.description: ## What Since #34273 a `type: 'script'` action can declare a `refusals` catalogue, and the server answers a refusal in the request's `Accept-Language`. That works — but **one throw answers exactly one declared sentence**: one `code`, at most one `reason`, one flat `params` object. An action that checks a whole selection and refuses all-or-nothing has several things to say at once — one sentence per offending record, each with its own reason and its own values. That answer cannot be expressed through the catalogue, so such an action has to choose between a list in the author's language and a single reason in the person's language. The resolver is shared with hooks (`resolveSandboxedRefusal`), so a hook that wants to name several reasons in one refusal meets the same limit. Only the action side was measured. ## Where we hit it HotCRM 6.6.0, `crm_expense.submit_for_reimbursement` and `submit_trip_for_reimbursement` (one shared script body). A person selects expenses and submits them; when some cannot go, nothing is submitted and the answer lists why, today as English literals: In a zh-CN console the person reads this in English (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2759). Moving it into `refusals` is not possible without either dropping the list or leaving it untranslated. ## Measured on 18.6.0 Booted stack through `@objectstack/verify`, `POST /api/v1/actions/crm_expense/submit_for_reimbursement`, once with `accept-language: en` and once with `zh-CN`. Probe catalogue on the action, with zh-CN rows under `objects.crm_expense._actions.submit_for_reimbursement.refusals.…`: | The body throws an `Error` carrying | Answer | |---|---| | `{ code: 'PROBE_PLAIN' }` | 400, `declaredCode: PROBE_PLAIN`; `Probe plain sentence.` / `探针：普通句子。` — works | | `{ code: 'PROBE', reason: 'on_report', params: { name: 'Taxi 12', count: 3 } }` | 409; `Expense Taxi 12 is already on an expense report (3).` / `费用 Taxi 12 已在报销单上（3）。` — works | | `params.name = ['Taxi 12', 'Hotel 7']` | the array is rendered as JSON: `Expense ["Taxi 12","Hotel 7"] is already on an expense report (2).` | | `reason: ['on_report', 'approved']` | ignored — the entry sentence, once | | `reasons: [ … ]` | ignored — the entry sentence, once | | `refusals: [ { code, reason, params }, … ]` | ignored — the entry sentence with empty holes: `Probe entry x.` | | `params: [ { … }, { … } ]` | ignored — holes empty | | an undeclared reason or code (computed at run), no code with its own `userMessage`, a plain `Error`, an `AggregateError`

items.title: feat: honour the envelope's step limit and wind down with a hand-off summary when it is reached
items.description: ## Problem The loop allows 10 LLM calls and the number cannot be changed. `TaskEnvelope.max_tool_iterations` (`marvin/models.py:105`) is never read: `AgentRunner.run` uses its own default (`marvin/runner.py:129`) and neither `entrypoint.py` nor `worker.py` passes the envelope value. Ten turns is too few for clone, explore, edit, test and open a PR. At the cap the loop makes one more call with the `tools` parameter removed (`anthropic_client.py:245-253`). On Anthropic that sends history containing `tool_use` blocks without tool definitions, which the API is expected to reject; nothing tells the model it is out of steps or asks for a summary. Reference behaviour: - opencode `core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:261-280` and `runner/max-steps.ts`: at the limit, a fixed prompt is appended asking for a summary of what was done and what remains, tool choice is set to none, and tool definitions stay in the request so the cached prefix still matches. - pi has no turn limit in its main harness; its durable harness ends a run as `unanswered` with reason `turn_limit` (`durable/src/harness/generation.ts:1274-1306`). Reference commits: pi `badlogic/pi-mono@a40abec`, opencode `sst/opencode@1017760` (both 2026-11-11). Paths below are relative to each repo's `packages/`. marvin paths are on `main` (`b0bc11c`). ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `TaskEnvelope.max_tool_iterations` controls the loop in both entry points (`entrypoint.py`, `worker.py`) - [ ] The default is raised to a value suited to development tasks; the number and its rationale are stated on the PR - [ ] At the limit the worker makes one final call that keeps the tool definitions, disables tool use, and instructs the model to report completed work, remaining work and the state of the workspace - [ ] A tool call returned on that final turn is not executed - [ ] The run is reported as stopped at the step limit (outcome defined in the failed-runs issue) - [ ] Tests cover the limit with the scripted fake LLM, including the final-turn request shape for Anthropic ## Dependencies - #82 (shared loop) - Raising the limit safely also needs the tool-output cap and compaction issues filed alongside this one. --- ## Readiness Analysis (prepare) **Verdict:** Ready to plan once the open questions below are answered. #82 is closed, so nothing blocks the start. Suggested estimate: **complexity:medium** (currently `complexity:simple`; see rationale). ### Code findings (verified on current branch) - `run_tool_loop` is in `marvin/loop.py`

items.title: Expose Goal controls outside the interactive TUI, both for external automation and agent-side workflows.
items.description: ### What variant of Codex are you using? CLI ### What feature would you like to see? Feature request: expose Goal controls outside the interactive TUI, both for external automation and agent-side workflows. Current behavior: - `/goal resume` works in the interactive TUI. - `codex exec resume "resume the goal..."` resumes the thread, but does not flip the internal Goal state from paused/blocked to active. - Prompting the agent to resume the goal is therefore not equivalent to the `/goal resume` slash command. - The agent can call `get_goal()` and observe goal status, timeUsedSeconds, tokensUsed, etc., but cannot resume or pause the goal through a tool. Why this matters: I want to automate long-running Goal work while respecting usage/rate limits. The clean path would be a scheduler or `codex exec resume`, but Goal mode currently requires manual TUI intervention to resume. Without a noninteractive Goal control, the fallback is brittle UI automation such as sleeping and using xdotool to type `/goal resume` into the TUI. Requested external/API surface: Please add documented noninteractive Goal commands, for example: - `codex goal status --json` - `codex goal resume ` - `codex goal pause ` - `codex goal clear ` Or equivalent flags on `codex exec resume`, for example: - `codex exec resume --goal-resume "continue working..."` - `codex exec resume --goal-status --json` Requested agent-side tool surface: Please also consider exposing Goal lifecycle tools to the agent, complementing the existing `get_goal()` tool: - `resume_goal()` - `pause_goal()` - possibly `clear_goal()` - possibly `get_usage()` / `get_rate_limits()` for the same data shown by `/status` or `/usage` Useful semantics: - `resume_goal()` should resume an existing paused/blocked goal without changing the objective. - `pause_goal()` should pause work without marking the goal complete or blocked. - These tools should return the same accounting fields as `get_goal()`, including status, timeUsedSeconds, tokensUsed, and objective. - They should be available in both interactive sessions and `codex exec resume` runs, subject to policy. - Transitions should be auditable in the transcript, like `update_goal`. Concrete use case: A user wants to run bounded unattended Goal work from cron/systemd or another scheduler: 1. Resume the saved Codex thread. 2. Resume the existing Goal. 3. Let the agent work for a user-defined slice, e.g. 20 minutes of Goal time. 4. Have the agent pause/stop before the cap. 5. Repeat la

items.title: epic: weighing as reconciliation: breakdown, first-weigh cases, end-of-life weighings, length, carriers
items.description: The scale is the truth, and every weighing reconciles what ScadBuddy believed with what the scale says. A reading of a spool is filament plus an empty spool plus add-ons. ScadBuddy keeps the gross reading, splits it with the empty weight it knows (the insert type now, the carrier and parts of #7278 later), compares the filament with the grams left it expected from the ledger, and shows the breakdown and the drift. A new spool's first weighing derives the empty weight (#7280) or, when the reading is under the label weight, asks what is up. A spool's last weighing, when it is finished, respooled or damaged out, closes the books: started, consumed by the ledger, consumed by the scale, drift. Length from the sliced plate joins grams, so density checks the label. Owner's direction (2026-11-25): approach C. Reconciliation and the end-of-life weighings first, the empty weight from the insert type until a carrier exists, carriers (#7278) as the second slice. **Spec and slice A plan:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-weighing-reconciliation-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-25-weighing-breakdown.md` (PR #7687). Slices (spec §8): - [x] A. Weighing breakdown and drift on every weighing; the start gap of an added-full spool (#7682, PR #7717, merged 2026-11-25) - [x] B. First weighing under the label weight on a new spool: the choice (#7683, PR #7748, merged 2026-11-25) - [ ] C. End-of-life weighings: finished, respooled, damaged out; the lifetime reconciliation (#7684, PR #7844) - [ ] D. Length per print from the sliced plate; the grams, length and density check (#7685, PR #7865) - [ ] E. Carriers and add-ons as tracked units: #7278 (exists; blocked on inventory phase 3, #7068, which gives spools `filament_spools.unit_id`: the owner's ruling 7 on the phase-2 plan, 2026-11-23) Under the filament epic #6260.

items.title: feat(inventory): spool parts: shells and addons as tracked units, and a spool's empty weight from its parts
items.description: A spool's empty weight becomes its insert plus its installed parts. Shells (a Bambu reusable spool, a printed spool) and addons (an AMS mini adaptor, a back spacer) become inventory units of a built-in kind `spool_part`. They are installed on a spool's unit and removed from it, and each one is traceable. A full-spool weighing checks that the parts add up. `spool_part` items are not saleable by default. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-spool-parts-design.md`, approved by the owner on 2026-11-23. Blocked by #7067 (inventory core). Epics #6949 and #6260.

items.title: Integrate execution preflight, Guard and acceptance evidence across the canonical runtime
items.description: ## Goal Turn the repository-execution preflight foundation from PR #1435 into an enforced end-to-end contract across AUREN's canonical task intake, planning, tool dispatch, filesystem/GitHub writes, verification, evidence and resume paths. Use FileKit/FileOperations PRs #5 and #7 as the real regression workload. ## Integration work 1. **Canonical plan integration:** have the canonical execution plan carry implementation/governance/evidence repository identity, base SHA, target branch, allowed path scope, acceptance rows, required capabilities, validation plan and stopping condition. Reject missing fields before mutation. 2. **Universal write-boundary enforcement:** apply repository/path scope checks to actual write adapters (worktree, file, shell, GitHub, PR/branch and commit paths). Resolve symlinks/canonical roots and reject traversal, escapes, unexpected cross-repo writes and identity drift. The preflight contract alone is not a sandbox. 3. **Schema discovery and validation:** connect tool registry discovery to all dispatch paths; validate actual arguments recursively against discovered schemas; prohibit guessed parameters and fail closed on unsupported constraints. 4. **Capability proof:** record runtime, browser, build, test, CI, artifact and permissions availability with evidence. Distinguish unavailable, not applicable, skipped, blocked, failed and passed. 5. **Acceptance/evidence lifecycle:** canonical acceptance matrix maps requirement -> change -> positive/negative test -> browser/integration test where relevant -> artifact/source evidence -> exact SHA -> result -> residual risk. Persist via the existing canonical evidence ledger, not a parallel store. 6. **Execution-loop checkpoints:** checkpoint after planning, coherent edits, validation, PR creation and CI polling. On resume reconcile with remote truth and invalidate stale evidence automatically. 7. **Production-path testing:** use FileKit regression cases: production build/preview rather than dev server; PDF lock/unlock round-trip and wrong-password; browser worker/WASM; nested ZIP traversal/depth/size limits; workbook sheet collisions; malformed input; offline first run; cancellation and recovery. 8. **Review and release gates:** independent source review, exact-head required CI, review-thread resolution, scope/diff inspection and release documentation. items.title: Redesign: PhoneEditProfile — Edit profile
items.description: Part of #376. Area: `customer-app-v2/`. ## Design — implement exactly this Source of truth: `docs/redesign/screens/PhoneEditProfile.dc.html` (design canvas board **PhoneEditProfile**), renders in `docs/redesign/screens/png/PhoneEditProfile*.png` at commit `bd46030` (PR #330). **Default** ## What this screen does Edit profile — name and email. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Server-validated; email change follows the existing confirmation flow. - [ ] Every state above matches its design render at the same width (layout, copy, order, states). - [ ] English and French strings. ### Implementation rules (all apply) From the owner's spec (`docs/redesign/specs/unlimited-catalog-and-device-locking.md`) and `AGENTS.md`: - **Build exactly this design.** The PNGs above and the linked `.dc.html` are the source of truth for layout, copy, states and order. Don't restyle, re-word or add elements; if something can't be built as drawn, ask on this issue before changing it. - **No hard-coded catalogue data.** Bundle names, prices, validity, device slots and placeholders (`[PLAN n]`, `[PRICE]`, `[KIT PRICE]`, `[XAF]`…) come from the API. The values in the design are examples. - **The server is authoritative.** It prices every checkout, validates every bundle field, and stores an immutable snapshot of the terms; screens display the snapshot, never recompute it. Retries are idempotent. - **Unlimited data.** No data caps or data-remaining figures for Unlimited bundles; show time left and device slots. - **Validity starts at first activation** and is never restarted or extended by replacing a device or router. - **MACs come from RouterOS only** (observed at authenticated HotSpot sign-in). Never send or trust a client-supplied MAC. Show MACs masked. - **Archive, never cascade-delete.** Unpublish/delete blocks new checkout immediately; used bundles are archived; ending access is an explicit "Revoke". - **Wording:** Personal bundles "restrict sharing" (never "block" or "prevent"); Home WISP: household sharing through a supported WISP router, with no device count (no "up to 60" claim; owner, 24 Nov). - **i18n:** every string through `shared-app/i18n.js`, English and French. - **Design kit:** build from `shared-app/ui/` tokens and components; screens go in `customer-app-v2/` / `admin-app-v2/`. v1 stays frozen. - **Off limits:** `UI_V2_PERCENT`, `UI_V2_OFF` and other env vars in `render*.yaml`; authentication code; no new dependencies; no SMS/authenticator code paths; PIN or passkey only

items.title: Ship the app as a PWA at app.openpb.org
items.description: **Context:** The MVP's only first-party client is an installable web app (a PWA) at `app.openpb.org`. Native apps come later. The decision and the domain layout are recorded in an ADR in openpickleball/backend (openpickleball/backend#182). `openpb.org` stays the public site from `site/`. This changes the move in `plans/app-migration/plan.md`, which puts the app on `openpb.org` itself. **Tasks:** - Update `plans/app-migration/plan.md`: the app goes to `app.openpb.org`, and `openpb.org` keeps the public site. - Choose the adapter. The API is reached same-origin through `app.openpb.org/api/`, `/_allauth/`, and `/oauth/`, routed to Django by App Platform, so the app can be a static build if it needs no server of its own. Record the choice in the plan's Decisions section. - Web app manifest, icons from `brand-assets`, and a service worker that caches the app shell. - Sign-up, login, email verification, and password reset through allauth's headless `browser` client (session cookie and CSRF). Email links from the backend open pages on `app.openpb.org`. - Offline match entry: queue submissions in IndexedDB and send them when the app opens or the device is back online (iOS has no Background Sync). A retry that gets a 409 duplicate naming the player's own match counts as sent. - Generate the API client from the backend's OpenAPI document. **Done when:** the app installs from the browser on Android and iOS, a player can sign up and log in on staging, and `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` pass. New to the project? Read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/openpickleball/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and sign off your commits (`git commit -s`).

items.title: [C9.3] 卷 II/III 分析课选择题
items.description: This is by an automated agent, not a human. # C9.3 — 卷 II/III 分析课选择题 父 issue: #96（C9 大计划）。 状态: **planned**。 规模: `courses/analysis` 171 单元 / 1019 道练习（卷 II 343、卷 III 676）；约 240–290 个 KP；约 **900–1300 道题**；20–30 批。 ## 目标 给分析课建知识点与选择题库，使插件能按卷 II/III 出题；内容必须由课程源/标准库核验，不新增课程内容。 ## 范围 - KP 注册：16 章（II.1–III.9），按 1.4–1.8 KP/单元估 240–290 个。 - 题目：卷 II 先做（有理数/实数构造/完备性），卷 III 再做（序列/级数/连续/微分/积分）；每批 40–50 题，共 20–30 批。 - 每题 fields 同 `soko.choice-bank/1`；`source` 指向 `courses/analysis` 的单元/lib 行；`kps` 挂载；综合题按章目标。 - 每章至少 1 个 lesson + 2 张卡；术语进 glossary。 - 解析/覆盖工具复用 `courses/analysis` 的课程门禁与 `courses/set-theory/knowledge` 的 validate/coverage（不复制第二套）。 ## 验收 - `python3 courses/analysis/tools/check.py --json`：0 rejected / 0 solutions_open / 0 lib_open（题库不破坏课程门禁）。 - 题库 `validate` / `coverage` 对已注册 KP GREEN；综合题目标；engine selftest/simulate。 - 卷 II/III 的分批读数（题数、KP 数、批次）写进 issue/PR；不锁计数。 - 不自动生成题；每道题可复查 source。 ## 依赖 C9.1（规格/KP 方法）；建议 C9.2 流程跑通后再开；C9.0 的 dataset 供代码题，独立。 ## 不做什么 不改课程画布/解答；不改 engine/kernel；不做 set-theory（C9.2）；不做 Analysis II/测度论。

items.title: feat(trusty-mpm): tm whats-new and a once-per-version notice from tm doctor, fed by a curated per-release highlights file
items.description: New features go unnoticed: `crates/trusty-mpm/CHANGELOG.md` is dense (over 9,000 lines), and `tm doctor` checks health only. Nothing tells a user what is new or the one command to try. Done when: - A curated highlights file exists per release: 3-5 lines per feature, each with the command to try. - `tm whats-new` prints the highlights for the installed version. - `tm doctor` shows a one-line notice once per version, tracked by a last-seen-version store. Follows from the ADR 0077 evaluation (awareness is separate from presets). A dashboard card is out of scope here and depends on [#10896](https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools/issues/10896). items.title: feat(trusty-mpm): config schema_version plus preset diff and non-destructive update for seeded Architect files
items.description: Seeded Architect files (`il-schedule.json` and kin) carry no version, and fleet init keeps an edited copy untouched. A new preset therefore never reaches existing installs, and an edited file has no way to see what changed. Done when: - Each seeded config file carries `schema_version`. - `tm config diff` compares the on-disk file with the current embedded preset. - An update applies preset changes without overwriting user edits, through a versioned migration step (ADR-0067 style). - A test covers an edited file surviving an update. Implements ADR 0077 (proposed; PR to follow). Relates [#10571](https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools/issues/10571), [#10608](https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools/issues/10608). Proposed by Maciek (Slack, relayed by Bob). 🤖🤖🤖 Generated with trusty-mpm — https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools

items.title: feat(trusty-mpm): tm il config show|enroll|set with a built-in il-schedule preset and a session example
items.description: Architect IL scheduling has no write path. `il-schedule.json` is seeded with `"sessions": []` and edited by hand; a user cannot learn the per-session schema from a blank list, and no `tm` verb edits it. Done when: - `tm il config show` prints the effective schedule. - `tm il config enroll ` and `tm il config set` edit sessions and thresholds; the CLI is the only writer. - `tm il config reset` restores the built-in il-schedule preset, which is embedded in the binary and works for the common case. - The preset carries one documented session example, and docs for it are generated from the preset, with a CI check that they match. Implements ADR 0077 (proposed; PR to follow). Relates [#9995](https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools/issues/9995), [#10116](https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools/issues/10116). Proposed by Maciek (Slack, relayed by Bob). 🤖🤖🤖 Generated with trusty-mpm — https://github.com/bobmatnyc/trusty-tools

items.title: Ask HN: Where are all the amazing AI-generated software?
items.description: I feel like the most amazing thing about AI so far is AI itself. Is anyone using a brand-new tool that was not available 5 years ago? I see people decompiling/reverse engineering the Adobe suite, which is an amazing feat, but the resulting software itself is barely usable. Since it’s so easy to build anything now, I get a sense we’re seeing a proliferation of one-off, proof-of-concept projects, where great software takes time and effort and often multiple people, AI notwithstanding.

items.title: Ask HN: For professional Mathematicians –- about your career in the future
items.description: Hi friends, genuine question. We all see that top notch Mathematicians can use LLM to prove world class results in a relatively short time of period. OK I admit some of the results are not verified yet, but please hear me. Neither do I know how much “brain” is human and how much is the LLM, because we don’t see the prompts. My question is: what do you think about your career in the future? Please hear me out. In the current world, the way you become a Mathematician, is to get good scores, go to schools, take PHD and then professorship. There may be middle steps like postdoctoral or industry experience, but that’s the general way to do it. And the way that schools judge professors, if I understand correctly, is more about how much results you can get —- ofc if you can obtain big grants then the better, but most of you can’t do that, so I assume that it’s more about the papers. You also teach but that’s not as big as the research. For now, there are a lot of smaller problems left to solve, and since world class Mathematicians tend to devote their life to one world class problem, there are plenty of food for everyone. Does the above make sense? This leads me to the question of: if the future of getting proofs is to prompt with an LLM or whatever AI solution, and it is apparent that world class Mathematicians can prove more conjectures or whatever than they ever can dream without LLM, why do schools need mediocre Mathematicians? I’m not trying to belittle you, but I’m trying to figure out career paths for my son, and I need to understand the impact of AI to all career paths. Again, I iterate, if one world class Mathematicians can prompt through many problems in their lifetime, we face two possibilities: 1. LLMs are good at solving problems but not good at asking new questions, so eventually we have few questions to crack, so the world doesn’t really need that many Mathematicians. 2. LLM is equally good at asking new questions. Well again I don’t see why the school needs to hire so many Mathematicians. Again, I believe LLM is merely the tool here, you still need the Mathematicians to do the thinking —- this does NOT contradict what I wrote. Of course, there is another part of your work, that is to teach Mathematics. But I’m not sure that is unique to humans. Maybe LLM can do that too. items.title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do?
items.description: I'm Senior software engineer in the US (DMV area), with 15y of experience. Worked for Fortune 50+ company and bunch of mid-size companies. Been unemployed for 2y and can't find a job, within those 2 years, I pretty much spent my savings that I've saved through years, maybe have 4-5 months left to support my household. Currently, I tutor math and probably about to start working as manager in pizzaria. In Jan 2025, I quit from a mid-size insurance tech company(1000+) after working there for almost 4y, because I was tipped off the they were about to start layoffs and they did. Well, since then I have zero luck finding any job in SWE. At this point, I have massive gap in my resume that I can't explain to recruiters, I can still code (C#/.NET/AWS) and learned the AI, but who cares if date of my last employment is Jan2025. What should I do ? If you have an alternative path (something completely different from SWE or SWE adjacent) that pays "well", I would like to hear.

items.title: Ask HN: Am I the only one whose AI hype is cooling down a lot?
items.description: I am in the industry for 15+ years, studied CS, and actually, never really "liked" programming. It was a means to an end. I have written about programming (and published books), so don't get me wrong: I like the craft and I miss the sense of accomplishment after hours and days of struggling and fixing a problem with 2 lines of code. What I see in my personal spending and habits: I get free tokens from my company, and I spent between 3k-5k a month at the start of the year. Models got cheaper, but also: The usefullness ran its course a little bit for me. I still don't write code by hand, but when doing research, finding solutions, even some decisions (using Opus 5.5 and Astra 6.2 for example) are more and more questionable. I handed large research tasks to models, but even small questions like: "What do you think about these PR comments pointing out issues" (I need to be vague, working for a larger company), it didn't find even basic facts I found via Google and reading the docs for 2mins. I usually did higher level thinking, researched with the model, and then went to the implementation phase. But lately, I am not happy with both the research results (I continuesly have to narrow it down, go back, refine... I spend a day or 2 days refining, which in the end, I can do by myself now and actually feel a sense of accomplishment). Even the implementation isn't all that great. Maybe my bar for acceptable work is higher now, since these tools are not "magic" anymore. I think I gave them more leeway in the beginning because they wowed me. But now... not so much anymore. I even dread opening up Claude Code or Codex and I'd rather read and write code myself, and just give them smaller tasks, or once I nailed it down, I let a large chunk of code write by a model (because it "types" faster...). Am I alone? I read a lot of think pieces, I have agents working on my private dedicated server to maintain my machine and set up my self-hosting services. But more and more, I'd rather.... do it myself again, be more precise, and use it as a workhorse instead of a thinking researcher.

items.title: Ask HN: Coworker rejects PR (a month in) because it does not meet his standards
items.description: just joined this new team about 1 year into their development. Demoed the work to the team about two weeks ago (half way in). Work is practically complete & runs well no issues. I create PR & assign the two PR reviewers (one my rank another a rank above me). one colleague (the one at my level) leaves some constructive comments no functional changes. The other colleague (one rank above me) says something equivalent to "does not meet our standards" "do not do x pattern since we have used y (which has a huge limitation)" to use Y pattern I would basically need to change most of the logic and it would be about 70% waste. I demoed my code with this pattern two weeks ago and there were no issues/comments from the team. The code is concise and easy to read. I had a call with the colleague and explained the code and why I used it, and showed him some other parts of the codebase where this pattern should be used, his only defense was that "it does not meet our standards because it uses X rather than y pattern, since we used y pattern in the past, we should only use y pattern" while x pattern is very similar only removing the limitation that was causing the code to be difficult to maintain etc. This "standard requirement" is written nowhere as a hard requirement and the codebase is barely one year old, with only one of the codebase founders still on the team.... I'm going to have a chat with the manager tomorrow morning.

items.title: Ask HN: Everything will get breached. How do you limit the blast radius?
items.description: Got another breach email this morning, this travel operator had my passport number and travel history stored. At this point I feel every service we use is going to get dumped eventually. I consider unique passwords and hardware 2FA as no brainers, they stop credential stuffing, but they don't help when a service leaks your actual identity. There are just so many services that require personal data like your passport number, phone number etc. And I think the fallout will only get worse as agentic workflows and local models become more mainstream and people start giving them more and more personal data. Assuming every vendor database is basically public eventually, how are you actually limiting the blast radius without turning everyday life into a massive faff?

items.title: Ask HN: How are tech recruiters assessed on their recruiting skills?
items.description: I've been working in tech for around 10 years but I have absolutely no experience at all in tech recruiting. However I have had the experience (well, often displeasure) of going through tech recruiters and the tech hiring process when applying for jobs during my career. As with probably many of you, I'm quite frustrated with how tech hiring has been in the last year or two during the AI/LLM era. It's incredibly frustrating to send tens to hundreds of CVs for applications you would be an excellent fit for and seeing the roles go to less qualified candidates, or candidates who just end up leaving after a few months or a year. This has left me wondering how tech recruiters are assessed on their recruiting skills and retaining qualified talent within their respective organizations. For those of you who work or have worked in tech recruiting, or have insider knowledge regarding how tech recruiters are assessed, could you share some insight into how tech recruiters are assessed? Is there any kind of follow-up regarding the performance of the people have hired, retention rates, and so on?

items.title: Ask HN: Is Anthropic being public better or worse for your org?
items.description: Now that Anthropic has a "fiduciary duty to maximize shareholder value"*, have you or your org started thinking about what that means medium to long term? For example, if you are using their models in production or production-adjacent systems, how do price changes impact your business? * I know they have a complicated governing system, but at the end of the day they have different pressures now than when they were private.
